html: Realizing empowerment as a real-time intrinsic drive imposes a demanding set of computational requirements. Unlike a simple reward signal that can be read off a scalar afferent (e.g., blood glucose), empowerment is a derived information-theoretic quantity: it requires the agent to internally represent a causal model of its own action-outcome channel, estimate entropies over high-dimensional future state distributions, and solve an optimization over action distributions–all before empowerment can even serve as a motivational signal to guide policy selection.
